locality: 25 km south of Taree, lower north coast of New South Wales
vegetation: Dry sclerophyll woodland with Eucalyptus racemosa subsp. racemosa dominant in the canopy, on comparatively well drained beach ridges.
georeference_remarks: Coordinates are those given for the Nabiac barriers as a whole (32°09'S, 152°26'E).
source_section: Study site and study species, p.255; Results, Climate and groundwater depth, p.257
notes: MAP is the long-term mean for Taree. Watertable at a mean depth of ~2.7 m for the first 4 months of the study, rising to 1.63 m after high rainfall in April 2008; capillary fringe ~0.4 m above the watertable. Beach ridge chronosequence spanning two interglacial cycles (80 000-260 000 years before present).
